This visualiser uses cranial and facial bones plus the mandible from BodyParts3D / Anatomography 4.3, obtained through the BodyParts3D mesh mirror. No tooth meshes are included.

Changes: selected bones, rotated and scaled coordinates, converted mesh format, simplified surfaces into flat triangular facets, added facet separation and artistic materials, jaw articulation and audio-driven deformation. The adapted geometry remains under CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan.

Detailed provenance and bone list · Adapted skull geometry · Adapted jaw geometry

Binary geometry consists of six little-endian float32 values per vertex: x, y, z, normal x, normal y, normal z. Each three vertices form a triangle.

Mitsuhashi N et al. BodyParts3D: 3D structure database for anatomical concepts. Nucleic Acids Research (2009). doi:10.1093/nar/gkn613.
